hook.text: The riff that opens 'Ye Entrancemperium' was lifted from an unfinished Mayhem track that sits on a bootleg.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: October to December 1996, Grieg Hall, Bergen, Norway

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Ihsahn (vocals, guitar, synthesizer), Samoth (guitar), Alver (bass), Trym (drums and percussion)

sentences.text: The liner notes credit Mayhem guitarist Euronymous all the same, though he had died three years earlier, before the album was made.
A 1996 EP called Reverence came out ahead of the album as its teaser, and it included 'The Loss and Curse of Reverence'.
Pytten handled the engineering and production.
Yens and David Palser did the sleeve photography, Stephen O'Malley did the sleeve design, and Christophe Szpajdel made the illustrations and logo.
Set against In the Nightside Eclipse, the band's previous album, this one plays faster and leans harder on guitar.
There are fewer keyboards, more clean singing and blast beats in the drums.
In 1998 a remastered version came out with the three Reverence tracks that had not made the album.
The band also made a promo video for 'The Loss and Curse of Reverence'.

listen_for.text: It is an orchestral version of 'Inno a Satana', so what you hear is an orchestra.
